problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[-i,i]\times {1-i}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

feedback.problem: Let $I=[-1,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [-|i|,|i|].$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the union of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *at least one* set:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for at least one}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=-0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{-0.5}={-0.5}\times [-0.5,0.5]={(-0.5,k)\,:\,k\in [-0.5,0.5]}.
$$

This represents a vertical line segment from the point $(-0.5,-0.5)$ to the point $(-0.5,0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/b7793d85e02ccd05c55c34971c90be087d58274eabd21f46fe09f08ccd60797b.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}={i}\times [-|i|,|i|]={(i,k)\,:\,k\in [-|i|,|i|]}
$$

is the vertical line segment from the point $(i,-|i|)$ to the point $(i,|i|).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/c30712295adfe51c655662cc09f8f1e23b3ea97573693154e0e0b6ba48e15c07.png)

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following figure that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/8ce0c60aafe1a41b372c1f1477241c584d6f8ae224113c360576feb37fc25a8c.png)
